en.p: There is a basket containing at least 10 white balls and at least 10 black balls, and an empty pouch. Using one die, the following trial is performed.

box: if the number rolled is 5 or more, put 2 white balls from the basket into the pouch;
if the number rolled is 4 or less, put 1 black ball from the basket into the pouch.

en.p: When this trial is repeated 5 times, let $a_n$ and $b_n$ be the numbers of white and black balls, respectively, in the pouch after the $n$th trial $(1\le n\le 5)$. Given that $a_5+b_5\ge 7$, the probability that there exists a natural number $k\ (1\le k\le 5)$ with $a_k=b_k$ is $\dfrac{q}{p}$. Find the value of $p+q$. (Here $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
